scenario-the-formation.summary: A divided Assembly reaches its formation deadline. A limited caretaker keeps existing policy running while the choice passes to a national election.

provisions.label: Government formation and the fallback election

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet
Read next: The Coalition — replacing a sitting Consul

scenario-the-audit.summary: A Territory completes the successful audits required for Statehood. Publication of the second qualifying audit brings the constitutional change into effect.

provisions.label: The Statehood Audit and admission requirements

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet
Compare: The Third Strike — audits of an existing State
Follow Korda — where concurrent petitions complicate the path

scenario-ordinary.summary: Public records, social provision, asylum procedures, and independent monitoring shape an ordinary week. The story follows the people who rely on those institutions.

links.label: Keep the Fiscal Architecture Quick Sheet

scenario-the-coalition.summary: Opposition to a Civic Consul does not itself install a government. A constructive vote must unite an absolute majority behind a named successor in the same vote.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet
Compare: The Formation — choosing a government after an election

scenario-the-second-path.summary: A successful citizen initiative can enact lawful reforms, but popular approval cannot authorize an appropriation that the initiative power excludes. Later legislation remains subject to constitutional disclosure duties.

provisions.label: Citizen initiative and its constitutional limits

links.label: Compare: The Organized Third — repealing an existing law
Read next: The Severed Clause — an initiative’s lawful remainder
Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-second-declaration.summary: Renaming an emergency does not evade the bar on relabeled continuation. The Monitor publishes an assessment; judicial review and the prohibition on discriminatory emergency measures remain available.

provisions.label: Absolute rights and discriminatory emergency measures

links.label: Keep the Rights & the Non-Derogable Floor Quick Sheet
Compare: The Void Exception — an amendment meets an absolute right
Read next: The Order — refusing an unlawful instruction

scenario-the-referendum.summary: A State’s independence referendum starts a process rather than completing it. Chamber approval, a national vote, and a ratified separation agreement are still required; failure at a later voting stage can end the petition.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet
Compare: The Petition — devolution within the Republic
Compare: The Departure — an Associated Community’s different right to leave

scenario-the-third-strike.summary: Three consecutive overall audit failures put an existing State into Provisional status. The State keeps its government and rights; an advisory council supports remediation, while devolution requires a separate process.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet
Read next: The Restoration — returning to ordinary State status
Compare: The Audit — a Territory’s route to Statehood

scenario-alliance-clause.summary: A ratified defense treaty supplies authorization when its stated trigger is met. The Court checks that trigger, while appropriations and treaty withdrawal remain separate legislative powers.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-automatic-floor.summary: A missed budget deadline activates the constitutional interim appropriation. It preserves the specified services while the Legislature remains responsible for resolving the budget impasse.

links.label: Keep the Fiscal Architecture Quick Sheet

scenario-coordination-failure.summary: Two executives can disagree while acting within their own domains. Council coordination and public recording expose the dispute; implementation still requires the institutions with lawful authority to act.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-critical-finding.summary: An adverse legislative audit creates a public finding, not an automatic sanction or a power to compel a response. The story tests the political force—and limits—of scrutiny on a permanent record.

links.label: Keep the The Monitors Quick Sheet

scenario-deadlock.summary: When the two Speakers cannot jointly nominate an Executive Monitor General within the prescribed window, selection passes to the Senate. Public confirmation remains a separate requirement.

provisions.label: Monitor General Term Expiry and Incapacity

links.label: Keep the The Monitors Quick Sheet

scenario-finality-act.summary: The Legislature can allocate jurisdiction, but it cannot leave a concrete constitutional injury without a court to hear it. Sensitive evidence changes how review proceeds, not whether a remedy is available.

provisions.label: Right to Courts and Legal Remedy

links.label: Keep the The Judiciary Quick Sheet

scenario-first-nomination.summary: A timely Senate rejection leaves the judicial nomination process running with temporary service preserving the Court’s work. Rejection does not trigger the bypass reserved for a missed voting deadline.

links.label: Keep the The Judiciary Quick Sheet

scenario-harder-ballot.summary: A voting-access restriction can face both a citizen’s rights challenge and independent election-compliance scrutiny. Those routes reinforce one another while addressing different constitutional duties.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-long-count.summary: Lottery selection does not replace public consent. Rejected Judicial Monitor candidates lead to renewed selection, while acting arrangements preserve the institution’s work.

provisions.label: Monitor General Term Expiry and Incapacity

links.label: Keep the The Monitors Quick Sheet

scenario-organized-third.summary: Citizens can organize to repeal an eligible law through the optional referendum. A successful repeal does not permanently prevent the Legislature from legislating again—or citizens from challenging the new law by referendum.

links.label: Keep the Amendments & Direct Democracy Quick Sheet

scenario-recalled-senator.summary: State recall, Senate vacancies, and judicial remedies are distinct questions. The legal resolution must respect elected service and the constitutional limit of two senators per State.

links.label: Keep the Recall & Removal Quick Sheet

scenario-sponsoring-state.summary: State participation in the immigration pathway does not make issued federal credentials dependent on continuing State approval. State discretion remains constrained by equality and access to legal remedy.

links.label: Keep the Immigration & Asylum Quick Sheet

scenario-the-administrator.summary: After material election non-compliance and an expired cure period, the Elections Panel can administer the federal election directly. A dispute about administration does not erase the votes cast.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-the-cause.summary: Misconduct can support removal of a Supreme Court justice; disagreement with a ruling cannot. Review of constitutional grounds does not substitute for the required removal votes in both chambers.

links.label: Keep the The Judiciary Quick Sheet

scenario-the-classification.summary: Classification must satisfy its lawful grounds. Monitor access and staff publication help expose misuse, but an oversight finding is distinct from an enforceable legal remedy.

links.label: Read Article X — The National Record System

scenario-the-contraction.summary: Certified Severe Revenue Contraction activates the National Endowment’s social-state backstop. Its restricted purpose and rules for continuation constrain how the reserve can be used during a fiscal shock.

links.label: Keep the Fiscal Architecture Quick Sheet

scenario-the-departure.summary: An Associated Community can terminate its Compact without Republic consent, on the required notice. Ending the Compact leaves transition obligations to resolve and does not itself extinguish members’ Republic citizenship.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-direction.summary: Publication makes an executive direction visible, but accountability depends on several institutions acting within their powers. Conflict rules, judicial review, refusal of unlawful orders, and political removal serve different purposes.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-the-formula.summary: A fiscal-equalization failure requires a published legislative response. The story follows the gap between a funding model and actual delivery, showing why repeated scrutiny matters even after a formula changes.

provisions.label: The Social State and Monetary Authority

links.label: Keep the Fiscal Architecture Quick Sheet

scenario-the-founding-choice.summary: An indigenous nation’s founding choice distinguishes a sovereign Compact relationship from Territorial Integration. The no-inducements rule protects that choice; the two relationships do not carry interchangeable exit rights.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-graduation.summary: A change of address tests voting access in everyday life. Administrative verification must respect the franchise and direct NVS access; the story’s processing time is not a constitutional waiting period.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-the-holdout.summary: Senate inaction can open a public-confirmation route that a timely rejection would not. Senate confirmation of a Judicial Pool nominee before the public vote is certified ends that bypass.

links.label: Keep the The Judiciary Quick Sheet

scenario-the-ledger.summary: Campaign source restrictions, contribution limits, and disclosure work together. Published records make a disguised funding pattern examinable; enforcement still runs through the responsible institutions and statutory procedures.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-the-map.summary: A Monitor’s criticism of a district map is informational. Citizens retain a route to challenge, and the Elections Panel’s interim-map duty supplies a separate backstop when a map fails the constitutional criteria.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-the-objection.summary: A fiscal notice records a concern and gives the Assembly Speaker an option to recall the bill. It is not a veto: declining recall leaves the warning on the record without giving it independent blocking force.

links.label: Keep the Article III — The Legislature Quick Sheet

scenario-the-order.summary: The duty to refuse concerns unlawful orders, not personal disagreement. A lawful refusal is protected against penalty; investigation and the institutions responsible for remedy make that protection effective.

provisions.label: Right to Courts and Legal Remedy

links.label: Keep the Rights & the Non-Derogable Floor Quick Sheet

scenario-the-petition.summary: Devolution changes a State’s relationship within the Republic. A referendum, negotiated agreement, and Senate ratification are distinct steps; becoming a Territory opens the re-qualification pathway rather than guaranteeing immediate Statehood.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-prior-claim.summary: Constitutional membership and an indigenous Compact relationship confer different powers. Federal technical standards must also be distinguished from commandeering State agencies to administer federal programs.

provisions.label: Acknowledgment of Prior Sovereignty and Recognition

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-rate.summary: Monetary independence protects constitutional functions, not every detail of statutory organization. Reorganization cannot become a way to punish lawful policy judgment or undermine protected decision-making.

links.label: Keep the Fiscal Architecture Quick Sheet

scenario-the-redaction.summary: A lawful period of classification does not make every page secret. A person can seek segregable public material and reasons for withholding; Monitor findings can inform a case without becoming disclosure orders.

provisions.label: Right to Courts and Legal Remedy

links.label: Read Article X — The National Record System

scenario-the-restoration.summary: Two consecutive fully clean annual audits restore ordinary State status by constitutional operation. This is the restoration of an existing State, not a Territory’s admission to Statehood.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-return.summary: Border-security authority remains subject to equality and legal remedy. The story also exposes a procedural question about returning credential holders that requires statutory clarity rather than an invented constitutional rule.

links.label: Keep the Immigration & Asylum Quick Sheet

scenario-the-second-renewal.summary: An extended military commitment must confront how it ends. The required Transition and Reconstruction Plan makes continuing authorization depend on an approved account of the Republic’s obligations across executive domains.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-the-severed-clause.summary: An initiative’s success does not authorize it to narrow protected rights. The Court identifies the specific constitutional conflict while leaving the lawful remainder of the voters’ decision in effect.

provisions.label: Privacy, Property, and Security of the Home

links.label: Keep the Amendments & Direct Democracy Quick Sheet

scenario-the-sixty-percent.summary: Removing a National Trust designation requires both legislative and public approval at the constitutional thresholds. A referendum majority below the required threshold leaves the designation and stewardship duty in place.

links.label: Keep the States, Territories & Indigenous Nations Quick Sheet

scenario-the-suspension.summary: Initiating a Monitor General’s removal suspends authority, not pay or the term. The public decides removal; failure or a missed referendum deadline restores authority under the constitutional process.

provisions.label: Monitor General Term Expiry and Incapacity

links.label: Keep the The Monitors Quick Sheet

scenario-the-three-hours.summary: Succession takes effect at the constitutional triggering event even during a records outage. The NRS must record that actual moment as soon as possible; delayed publication does not create a vacancy.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-the-three-recusals.summary: Disclosure and recusal duties apply across offices, but their enforcement differs. Direct publication, challenges to affected decisions, workforce oversight, and prescribed removal procedures address different kinds of responsibility.

links.label: Keep the The Monitors Quick Sheet

scenario-the-twenty-four-hours.summary: Temporary incapacity suspends the exercise of authority while the Consul remains in office. A recurring determination raises the thresholds and opens judicial review; political removal remains a separate process.

links.label: Keep the Article II — The Dual Executive Quick Sheet

scenario-the-unremovable.summary: An unresolvable removal case still has a constitutional floor. Non-refoulement, judicial supervision, and the prohibition on indefinite stateless detention constrain the treatment of a person whose removal is not possible.

links.label: Keep the Immigration & Asylum Quick Sheet

scenario-the-vote.summary: A suspensive veto creates a bounded delay with specified routes back to enactment. A fiscal notice is a separate instrument, and replacing the Civic Consul does not bypass tabling attached to the bill.

links.label: Keep the Article III — The Legislature Quick Sheet

scenario-the-waiver.summary: The consular election’s 60% waiver uses the national ranked-choice result. It is distinct from the first-preference State plurality test, so transferred preferences can determine whether the waiver applies.

links.label: Keep the Elections & Electoral Finance Quick Sheet

scenario-void-exception.summary: A procedurally valid amendment can still contain a clause that extinguishes a non-derogable right. The Court applies the amendment while treating only the conflicting part as void.

links.label: Keep the Amendments & Direct Democracy Quick Sheet

scenario-the-first-twelve-years.summary: Three sovereign predecessor countries adopt the constitutional framework and use Article XIX to merge without a gap in rights, obligations, elections, courts, records, or ordinary public services.
